## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

- **Date:** 2026-10-01  
  **Source:** [OpenAI ChatGPT release notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI release notes say GPT-6.1 Sol is rolling out in ChatGPT Work and Codex, beginning with Pro users. The update emphasizes stronger agentic coding, computer-use, and professional-work performance, alongside “dots,” persistent always-on agents in ChatGPT with connected apps and a cloud computer for ongoing tasks.  
  **Why it matters:** This is a material shift from session-based assistant use toward persistent agent infrastructure inside ChatGPT/Codex.

- **Date:** 2026-10-01  
  **Source:** [OpenAI API changelog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI added GPT-6.1 Sol to the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, added computer-use support for hosted Agents API browser tasks, and posted deprecations for GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.1, and GPT-5.4-Nano, scheduled for shutdown on 2027-04-01.  
  **Why it matters:** Developers have a clear migration path toward GPT-6-family models and should begin dependency audits for GPT-5-era model IDs.

- **Date:** 2026-10-02  
  **Source:** [OpenAI — A model guide for the GPT-6 family](https://openai.com/index/practical-guide-building-gpt-6)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI published implementation guidance for choosing GPT-6-family models, setting reasoning effort, improving prompts and skills, coordinating tools, and preparing production workflows.  
  **Why it matters:** The guide operationalizes GPT-6 adoption and indicates OpenAI is steering builders toward model-routing, tool orchestration, and production-agent patterns rather than single-model prompt use.
